topic: How does the 45° scan range affect link budget calculations for edge-of-coverage users compared to broadside beams?
consensus_response: A 45° scan range inherently introduces increased multipath interference, leading to signal attenuation and reduced link budget. This impacts SNR, impacting BER and throughput, and ultimately degrading latency-sensitive applications.  While broadside beams offer wider coverage and lower attenuation, 45° beams increase interference and require complex signal processing.  This trade-off necessitates a deeper understanding of noise characteristics and sophisticated signal processing techniques to mitigate interference and maintain optimal link budget and performance, especially for edge-of-coverage users.
